newsitem.title: MEXICO: Faulty data delays Mexico's natgas privatization.
newsitem.headline: Faulty data delays Mexico's natgas privatization.

text.p: The bidding process for natural gas distribution in Mexican industrial center Toluca has been delayed because of faulty government information, Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) president Hector Olea said on Wednesday.

A decision on the winner in the coveted privatization will be delayed to July 29 from July 9, because a government assesor incorrectly stated the amount companies were required to pay state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) in monthly fees, Olea told Reuters.
The assesor incorrectly stated that the fee would be double the actual amount in a statement distributed to participating companies, he said.

Because of the error, the CRE asked the six bidding companies to take back their economic offers for the concession and reconsider their bids by a new due date of July 10. The decision follows the CRE's review of the bids.
Bidders for the distribution concession include:
--Mexico's Centra Gas de Toluca, Canada's WestCoast Energy Inc. and U.S. Coastal Gas Toluca.
--France's Gaz de France Intl and Mexico's Mexigas.
--Mexico's Consorcio Sistema Automatico de Gas, Toluca Disco Holding and U.S. Enova Corp.
--Mexico's Grupo Mexicano de Desarollo SA, Canada's Gas International, and U.S. Shell Oil Company.
--U.S. Noram Energy Corp and Mexico's Gutsa Construcciones.
Toluca is the fourth and largest to date in a series of privatization of natural gas distribution rights. A total $100 million is expected in investments at the site.
